parsed.why: No criminalisation, but tier-1 exposures are operative: birth-sex strip-search, statutory single-sex exclusion code, ward bans, prison placement ruling, one documented death. Rule of law enforces hostile policy, not recourse.

No trans criminalisation, reformed legal recognition, rising acceptance, functioning courts. Exposures are border marker checks and diagnosis gatekeeping; documented violence incidents are a decade old, no current pattern against visitors.

Self-declaration recognition, comprehensive trans statute, hate-crime coverage, trans choosing prison placement, murderer prosecuted. Resident violence statistics and uneven service enforcement remain, but protections demonstrably operate.

Death-by-stoning/crucifixion sentences for same-sex conduct in 2024, modesty laws reaching public presentation, no discrimination protection, vigilante licence, factional enforcement. Outed visitor faces catastrophic, state-sanctioned severity.

Decriminalised but no recognition or discrimination law; documented 4x assault rate, police dismissing complaints because of male ID markers, healthcare refusals — hostility with thin recourse, though no criminal or custody exposure.
